newsitem.title: UK: Enterprise Inns expects to double beer sales.
newsitem.headline: Enterprise Inns expects to double beer sales.

text.p: Independent pub company Enterprise Inns said it expects to almost double beer sales and as a result has negotiated seven-year supply contracts with Britain's big four brewers.

The company acquired 413 managed and tenanted pubs in England and Wales owned by John Labatt (UK) Ltd (JLR) from Belgian brewers Interbrew Belgium SA for 51.3 million stg in June, adding hugely to its beer volumes.
"The key thing we were looking for as a result of doubling volumes was long term security," chief executive Ted Tuppen told Reuters in an interview.
"So we have now got seven-year terms with all the major brewers," he said.
He declined to quantify the discount. "The agreements were struck at very close to the top of the discount curve," he said.
Since the acquisition of the JLR estate Enterprise has converted all of the JLR managed pubs to tenancies and reduced overhead costs by closing the four JLR offices.
Earlier the company reported a 13 percent increase in profits before tax and exceptionals to 8.7 million in the year ended September 30.
Exceptional costs of 3.1 million stg related mainly to the cost of reorganising JLR. Enterprise assumed about 10.2 million stg of JLR debt as part of the acquisition.

The company, which was floated on the London stockmarket in November 1995 at 145p a share, currently has a leased and tenanted pub estate of about 1,000, including 98 pubs operated in a joint venture in the north west of England.
Enterprise shares stood 7-1/2p higher at 247p at 1430 GMT.
